answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence a shared reputation score. A mirror identity that copies an honest agent’s history still starts without that history, and attempts to farm trust through collusion risk losing the stake when independently sampled partners expose conflicting claims. The mechanism does not prove one person per account; it makes mass identities costly: an attacker must fund many locks and keep them tied up, while pigment and prism can serve as distinct labels in the audit trail, not as proof of uniqueness.
